newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caldera says Venezuela on road to recovery.
newsitem.headline: Caldera says Venezuela on road to recovery.

text.p: Venezuela, after four years of almost constant recession, is on the brink of regaining the prosperity that once made it one of Latin America's richest countries, President Rafael Caldera said on Thursday.
"We are marching on solid ground toward the conquest of the goals of wealth and national prosperity," he told troops guarding the border with Colombia in a traditional Christmas greeting.

Caldera, 80, who launched an economic reform program in April that ran contrary to several election promises, said that thanks to the measures "we have managed to overcome difficulties which appeared insurmountable."
The International Monetary Fund-inspired program increased gasoline prices by 500 percent, removed controls on currency trading and raised taxes.

While delighting the financial markets and attracting foreign investors, the economic plan has forced ordinary Venezuelans to tighten their belts in coping with the rising cost of living. Prices have increased by over 100 percent in the last year.
Caldera said his government would do its best to correct the wealth inequality. "Of course, our main concern is that the economic recovery is not exclusively for the privileged classes."
The largest oil reserves outside of the Middle East made Venezuela the envy of the continent in the 1970s and early 1980s when oil prices spiked.

But a drop in prices and mismanagement of the oil bonanza has seen the economy grind to a halt. Wages in Venezuela have not risen for over two decades in real terms, according to government officials.
